name: Larsen & Toubro Limited
summary: India's largest construction company — it builds highways, metros, bridges, ports and power plants, but does not usually own them.
about: L&T was started in 1938 by two Danish engineers, Henning Holck-Larsen and Søren Kristian Toubro, who were stranded in India by the Second World War and turned a small equipment agency into an engineering firm. It is now the company Indian governments call for the projects that are too big or too difficult for anyone else — expressway packages, long bridges, metro tunnels, airports and nuclear plants. On roads it is usually an EPC contractor: it is paid to design and build a stretch, then hands it over to the authority that owns it, rather than collecting toll itself.
facts: Founded in 1938 by two Danish engineers who stayed in India after the war began.
Builds highways, metro lines, bridges, ports, airports and power stations.
Usually paid to build a road rather than owning or tolling it afterwards.
Also built the Statue of Unity in Gujarat.
